assessment.nobel_worthiness: A rare chain from basic gut-hormone physiology (proglucagon processing, GLP-1 as an incretin and appetite signal) to therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity management. Originality, clarity of mechanism and breadth of clinical impact are all exceptional, and the effects reach cardiovascular and renal outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established GLP-1 physiology and its therapeutic rationale; Mojsov's work on the active peptide form is a decisive contribution that is credited but sometimes contested. Knudsen led the development of the durable analogues, but a three-person prize is most defensible around the physiological discovery. Allocation among these four, and the absence of other pioneers from this list, is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs and very large outcome trials. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue given the scale of use.
uncertainties: Credit among Mojsov, Drucker, Holst and the peptide chemists/developers is disputed in the literature and I cannot verify the details independently.
Whether the prize should honour physiology or drug development (Knudsen) is a genuine choice.
Long-term safety and durability of the weight effects are still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors created a new class of living therapy that produces durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies. The concept, its engineering and the clinical proof are clear and original, and it has opened a field of cell therapy.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain drove the design of costimulated CAR constructs and the first clinical successes; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Other early contributors (for example the originators of the chimeric receptor concept) are not on the credited list, so the configuration is plausible but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and over a decade of follow-up in leukemia and lymphoma. Solid-tumour efficacy is not yet established, but the core discovery is stable and widely confirmed.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept lies partly outside the supplied names.
Toxicity, relapse and limited solid-tumour activity remain open.
Whether Rosenberg's contribution is best described as foundational for CAR-T specifically.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience millisecond, cell-type-specific causal control of neural circuits and has become a standard tool for dissecting circuits underlying behavior, including motor and locomotor systems. Its methodological impact on physiology is vast. As a tool it is less a disease discovery, but the Nobel tradition does recognise enabling methods of this kind.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterised channelrhodopsin as a light-gated cation channel; Deisseroth (with Boyden) demonstrated its use in neurons and drove broad adoption. Bamberg and Miesenböck also made foundational contributions, and Boyden's role in the first neuronal demonstration is strong, so a three-person limit forces a difficult choice. I weight the molecular discovery plus the adoption.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of robust, independent replication and daily use worldwide. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: The three-laureate limit excludes at least two or three well-justified contributors; the allocation is genuinely contested.
Clinical translation (vision restoration) is still early.
I am drawing on general knowledge and cannot verify the relative priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-based antisense correction of SMN2 splicing turned a uniformly fatal infant motor-neuron disease into a treatable one. It is a compelling example of RNA biology leading directly to a transformative therapy, with a clear causal chain from splicing mechanism to nusinersen.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing regulatory elements and the antisense strategy; Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development with clinical translation. The pair is a clean and plausible configuration, though others in clinical development and in the broader antisense field may also merit consideration.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with years of real-world and long-term follow-up; effects in presymptomatic treatment are striking. The platform logic has been independently extended to other diseases.
uncertainties: Long-term outcomes in treated patients and the best dosing paradigms are still being defined.
Foundational antisense chemistry credit extends beyond the two credited names.
Possible overlap with later SMA therapies (gene therapy, small-molecule splicing modifiers) in how the prize would be framed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response revealed an organelle-to-nucleus signalling pathway that senses ER protein-folding load and adjusts gene expression. It is conceptually original, mechanistically clear and relevant to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory-cell physiology.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori delineated IRE1, the HAC1/XBP1 splicing mechanism and the pathway logic, a natural two-person configuration. Contributions from other groups on PERK/ATF6 branches are not reflected in the credited names, which leaves some attribution ambiguity.
assessment.maturity: Mechanisms have been confirmed in yeast and mammals for more than twenty-five years and are textbook material. Recognition is on time or somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Disease-level translation remains limited, so the case rests mainly on fundamental cell biology.
Credit for the mammalian branches beyond IRE1 may need to be weighed.
Recent overlapping prizes in protein homeostasis could affect framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and as a central regulator of growth and nutrient responses reshaped our understanding of cell growth, metabolism, ageing and cancer. The concept is fundamental and widely general.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified the TOR genes and their function in yeast; Schreiber's chemical genetics defined the FKBP12-rapamycin complex and mammalian target. Sabatini made key later contributions on mTORC1 nutrient sensing but his inclusion is complicated and the supplied credit set offers no unambiguous third; there are also other early contributors (for example in rapamycin discovery) not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and extensively confirmed, with rapalogs in clinical use and continuing expansion into metabolism and ageing.
uncertainties: Credit among the several groups that converged on the mammalian target is not fully settled in my knowledge.
Clinical impact of rapalogs is real but narrower than the biology's reach.
Whether the prize would be framed around the target discovery or the nutrient-sensing pathway.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib validated the principle of targeting an oncogenic kinase (BCR-ABL) in cancer and converted chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition. This is a landmark proof of concept for precision oncology.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the discovery and chemistry, Druker the clinical translation, and Sawyers extended the work to resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors. The configuration is clean; the discovery of BCR-ABL itself and the earlier cytogenetic work rest with others outside the list, which is a question of how the prize is framed.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of outcomes data and a template followed by many kinase inhibitors. Its impact is beyond question; the risk is that the field's peak recognition has already been through other awards.
uncertainties: The earlier BCR-ABL fusion discovery may be viewed as a precondition belonging to a different set of people.
Relative weighting of Sawyers' resistance work versus the discovery of the compound.
Whether the committee would prefer to reward the principle through a different, more recent targeted therapy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Recombinant virus-like particle vaccines against HPV demonstrated that a purely structural, non-infectious immunogen can prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers. The preventive medicine impact is large and, given population-level data on cervical lesions and cancers, increasingly clear.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 virus-like particles; Frazer contributed to the early VLP and vaccine development in parallel. Other groups worked on VLP assembly at overlapping times, so priority is not entirely clean, and the discovery that HPV causes cervical cancer was already recognised in 2008.
assessment.maturity: Widespread vaccination with population-level reductions in infection and high-grade lesions; evidence for reduction of invasive cancer is now accumulating strongly. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority disputes among groups developing VLPs, which I cannot verify from the supplied text.
Overlap with the 2008 prize for the HPV-cancer link might make the committee view this as secondary.
Long-term duration of protection and vaccine uptake effects are still being measured.
